title: Salvation through Faith Alone
definition: Salvation through Faith Alone teaches that sinners receive justification and salvation by trusting in Christ, not by earning righteousness.
summary: Salvation through Faith Alone teaches that sinners receive Christ and His benefits by trusting Him, not by works.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the object of saving faith and the only ground of acceptance before God.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Salvation through faith alone means sinners receive Christ and His benefits by trusting Him, not by adding works as the basis of acceptance. Scripture presents faith as the empty hand that receives grace.

Faith does not save because it is impressive in itself. Faith saves because it looks away from self and rests on Jesus Christ.

Jesus is the object of saving faith. The believer is not saved by faith in faith, but by faith in the crucified and risen Lord.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Troubled people often ask whether they have done enough, felt enough, or changed enough to be accepted. Faith alone directs the conscience away from self-measurement and toward Christ's finished work.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Place your confidence in Christ rather than in the strength of your own faith. When teaching others, make clear that faith receives salvation; it does not manufacture the righteousness God requires.
